The email also mentions physical certificate shipping arrangements; receipt of a hard-copy certificate is not independently documented. This is a competition ambassador distinction, not a Final Round participant medal.

cards.title: Organizer Commendation — IYMC 2026 Qualification Round

The team said the submission was among those being considered for possible display on the IYMC website. The message does not confirm a prize, qualification to another round, or actual publication as a featured submission. The individual correspondence is retained privately.

items.title: TruthLens: An Explainable Multi-Agent Framework for Hallucination Detection through Evidence-Based Verification in Large Language Models
items.abstract: TruthLens proposes a five-agent framework for detecting potentially hallucinated claims in large language model outputs through evidence retrieval, claim-level verification and explainable reasoning. The provided IJISRT reviewer report describes an auditable verification pipeline and evaluation considerations.
items.question: Can claim-level, evidence-grounded verification make LLM hallucination detection more transparent and interpretable?
items.method: The reviewer report describes five cooperating agents: Claim Extraction, Evidence Retrieval, Verification, Hallucination Assessment, and Explanation. It outlines evaluation using TruthfulQA, HaluEval, FEVER and HotpotQA, with attention to detection accuracy, evidence quality, explainability and computational overhead.
items.result: The supplied IJISRT reviewer report records Stage 1: Accepted and Stage 2: Accepted. An editor acceptance email dated 4 August 2026 states acceptance for publication subject to completing registration. Final public journal publication and paper-specific DOI have not been independently located.
items.publication: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT), planned Volume 11, Issue 8 (August 2026), subject to registration and final publication procedures.
items.details: TruthLens addresses hallucination detection in large language models through explainable, evidence-based multi-agent verification. The provided IJISRT four-page reviewer report describes supported, contradicted and unverifiable claim classification, confidence assessments and human-readable explanations. It notes limitations including computational latency, dependence on external evidence, threshold sensitivity, and multilingual challenges. The editor decision on page 4 is to accept the paper; the email states that publication follows completion of registration. Acceptance is distinct from confirmation of final journal publication.
items.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
items.reviewEvidence: Acceptance email and a 4-page IJISRT reviewer report were provided and reviewed. These are private supporting documents, not publicly hosted.
items.evidenceStatus: Acceptance documented; journal publication/DOI not independently confirmed
